solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soprano is wearing least exotic ornamental tuft

indicators.note: being worn means being wrapped round, so the rearranged word goes on the outside of the single letter
exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters of least are rearranged

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: A singer dresses in the least exotic decorative tuft available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' makes TASEL from LEAST, and 'is wearing' wraps that round S.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassel is a decorative bunch of hanging threads, as on a cushion or mortarboard.

clue.text: Staggering amount in an excess of products

indicators.note: staggering means reeling unsteadily, so the letters of amount lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: An astonishing quantity sits among a glut of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' looks like an adjective praising the amount, but it rearranges AMOUNT into MOUNTA; IN is added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists speak of a butter or wine mountain: a huge stockpile of surplus produce.

clue.text: Break veteran arranged after first of campaigns in operation

indicators.note: after places the rearranged veteran behind the other pieces
first of means only the opening letter of campaigns is used

parts.note: something in operation is on, as a machine switched on

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of veteran are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An old soldier, sorted out after the first campaign, breaks the rules on active service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' gives TRAVENE; 'after' puts it behind the other pieces, though the clue lists them in the opposite order. 'in operation' is the everyday sense of on, as a switched-on machine.
explanation.definitionFit: To contravene a law is to break or violate it.

clue.text: One that's revered by Irish excited reaction

parts.note: a saint is a revered person, abbreviated St

explanation.surface: A venerated figure from Ireland provokes an emotional response.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or flurry of public excitement.

clue.text: A set of drinks before a lot of dressing in a type of competition

parts.note: a round is drinks bought for the whole group at once

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: robing is putting on robes, dressing

explanation.surface: Buying a round before getting mostly dressed for some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims ROBING to ROBIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a tournament format in which every entrant plays every other.

clue.text: Choice fruit

definitions.meaning: choice as an adjective means excellent, highly desirable
a stone fruit with smooth purple skin

explanation.surface: A selected piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job is a choice, much-coveted one; the plum is also a familiar orchard fruit.

clue.text: A French medic is enveloped by cheers in Arctic environment

indicators.note: being enveloped means being wrapped inside, so the article and medic sit inside the word for cheers

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
un is French for a
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A French doctor, greeted with applause, working in the frozen north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' here means thanks, not applause: TA is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the treeless, frozen plain of the Arctic regions.

clue.text: Take a shine to Scandinavian ignoring European flashy sort

parts.note: to fancy someone is to take a shine to them

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letter for European is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: a Dane is a Scandinavian from Denmark

explanation.surface: Falling for a Scandinavian while overlooking a European show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' takes E out of DANE to leave DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy dan is American slang for a showy, ostentatious person.

clue.text: Stop with Oscar to acquire book and ring requiring quite a hefty sum?

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so the book and ring letters go inside the rest

parts.note: to abort a process is to stop it
a ring is round, like the letter O
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt a deal unless Oscar gets a book and a ring, at some cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to acquire' puts BO inside ABORTWO. The definition is ironic understatement, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob or two is British slang for a good deal of money, often said with understatement; bob was a shilling.

clue.text: Former aviation entrepreneur is more flamboyant by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: louder means showier, more garish

explanation.surface: An airline founder is said to be rather more showy.
explanation.walkthrough: Niki Lauda, the Austrian racing champion, founded the airline Lauda Air.
explanation.definitionFit: Niki Lauda, Formula One world champion, also founded and ran the airlines Lauda Air and Niki.

clue.text: Unusual reason to save time for a political representative

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe within, so the time letter is held inside
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of reason take an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange excuse for saving time, offered by a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' makes SENAOR from REASON; 'to save' holds T within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is an elected member of a senate, such as the US upper house.

clue.text: Wandering inspector enters much of Monaco nervously

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the inspector goes into the rearranged letters
nervously suggests jittery movement, so the letters are jumbled
much of means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written, the Mediterranean principality
DI is Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective moves anxiously into the principality of Monaco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much of' trims MONACO to MONAC; 'nervously' rearranges that to NOMAC, which DI 'enters'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomadic people roam from place to place with no settled home.

clue.text: Blue tag regularly found in pasture

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A blue label turns up in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic word for meadow or grassland.

clue.text: Initially, assistance is given face to face

parts.note: at first means initially, at the start
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: At the start, help is offered in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning something at first hand means directly, in person, without an intermediary.

clue.text: Support clubs, maybe, to do the same

parts.note: to follow a team is to support it
clubs is one example of a suit of cards, hence maybe

explanation.surface: Backing the football clubs, maybe, just as others do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like football teams to support; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games following suit means playing the led suit, hence copying others.

clue.text: Short drink supplied by fashionable place first off proves apposite

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
hep is an old form of hip, trendy

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: a joint is a place, as a club or restaurant

explanation.surface: A quick drink served at a trendy bar proves relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' takes J from JOINT, leaving OINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks that are to the point are relevant and pertinent, which is what apposite means.

clue.text: Something employed to an extent in turning point

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something used partly as a pivot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is the pivot on which a door turns, and figuratively a decisive point.

clue.text: Deceive English poet with women in front of kiosk

parts.note: Thomas Hood was a nineteenth-century English poet

indicators.note: front of means only the first letter of kiosk is used

explanation.surface: An English poet and some women standing outside a kiosk play a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink someone is to dupe or fool them.

clue.text: Lazy sort missing second shot from back of the court?

definitions.text: shot from back of the court?

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for second is taken away

parts.note: a slob is a lazy, untidy person

explanation.surface: A lazy player misses a second shot from the baseline.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a lob is a high stroke, often played from the baseline, over the opponent's head.

clue.text: Easy goal engineered in part without resistance

indicators.note: engineered means contrived or set up, so the letters are put in new order
without means lacking, so the resistance letter is dropped

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A simple score was set up in part with no opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes R from PART to leave PAT, which 'engineered' mixes with IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap-in is a goal scored with a light touch from very close range.

clue.text: Latin TV presenter tucks into French bread and fruit

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the two pieces go inside the French word

parts.note: pain is the French word for bread
Ant McPartlin, of the UK presenting duo Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A Latin American TV host eats French bread and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' suggests eating, but it is the insertion signal. Ant and Dec are a famous British TV presenting pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a banana-like fruit usually cooked before eating.

clue.text: Note one heartless bunch warring in succession

indicators.note: warring means in conflict, so the letters are thrown into disorder
heartless means the central letter of bunch is removed

explanation.surface: A cruel bunch at war, noted one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle N from BUNCH, leaving BUCH; 'warring' rearranges NOTE, ONE and BUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Wins on the bounce are wins in a row, one straight after another.

clue.text: Trustee defending poor working as lethargy

indicators.note: defending means guarding on both sides, so the abbreviation surrounds the rest
working means being worked into a new shape, so the letters of poor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trustee speaks up for a poor person, treating it as weariness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' turns POOR into ORPO, which TR is 'defending'.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor is sluggishness, a state of physical or mental inactivity.

clue.text: Prince in heart of Bath? That's fitting

indicators.note: in places the prince letter inside the middle letters
heart of means the central letters of Bath

explanation.surface: A prince at the centre of the city of Bath: how appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt and fitting both mean suitable or appropriate.

clue.text: Figure followed by worker is no permanent dweller

indicators.note: followed by puts the worker after the figure

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
the ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A number followed by a labourer has no fixed abode.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant rents a home rather than owning it, so occupies it only for a term.

clue.text: Recall gentleman with argument about online concerns

indicators.note: about means going around, so the backwards words surround the online letter
recall means calling back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: sir is a title or address for a gentleman
a row is a quarrel
E, as in e-mail, stands for electronic or online

explanation.surface: Recalling a quarrel with a gentleman about the internet causes anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' turns SIRROW into WORRIS; 'about' wraps it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Worries and concerns are both anxieties or causes of unease.

clue.text: Pair in site memorably

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words site memorably

explanation.surface: A couple visit a site that made a memorable impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people romantically linked are called an item, that is, a couple.

clue.text: Small bit of bread scattered on court

indicators.note: scattered means strewn about, so the letters of on and court are rearranged

explanation.surface: Breadcrumbs strewn across the court.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried or toasted bread for soups and salads.

clue.text: Chap found in mutual agreement (not half)

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the synonym is kept

parts.note: a covenant is a formal agreement binding both parties

explanation.surface: A man turns up in a contract, only half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: COVE is old British slang for a man, a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Cove is old British slang for a fellow or chap.

clue.text: Thing a cowboy might use shortly if returning close to cattle

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters of the synonym run backwards

parts.note: soon means shortly, in a little while

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of cattle

explanation.surface: A cowboy would use it soon when coming back near the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso has a running loop, and a noose is exactly such a slip-knotted loop.

clue.text: Meeting has institute replacing company? That's a lie

indicators.note: replacing means one letter group stands in for another

parts.note: a convention is a large formal meeting

explanation.surface: An assembly where an institute replaces a firm turns out to be false.
explanation.definitionFit: An invention can be a fabrication, something made up and untrue.
